items.stem: In MATLAB, what is the difference between A*B and A.*B for matrices of compatible size?

options.text: A*B is matrix multiplication; A.*B multiplies corresponding elements
options.rationale: Correct: * is the linear-algebra matrix product, while .* is element-wise.
They differ: one is a matrix product, the other element-wise.

options.text: A.*B is matrix multiplication; A*B is element-wise

options.rationale: A*B is defined for conformable matrices, not only scalars.

items.stem: Which statements about MATLAB arrays are correct? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: the first element of an array is A(1).

options.text: The colon operator can select an entire row or column
options.rationale: Correct: A(2,:) selects the whole second row.

options.text: Negative indices count from the end as in some languages
options.rationale: MATLAB uses the end keyword, not negative indices.

options.text: Scalars cannot be stored in arrays
options.rationale: A scalar is simply a 1x1 array in MATLAB.

items.explanation: Correct: the first element of an array is A(1).; Correct: A(2,:) selects the whole second row.

items.stem: Why is vectorising a computation usually preferred over an equivalent element-by-element for loop in MATLAB?

options.text: Vectorised operations run in optimised library code over whole arrays, so they are typically much faster
options.rationale: Correct: MATLAB's array operations are implemented in fast compiled routines, avoiding interpreter overhead per element.

options.text: Loops are not allowed in MATLAB
options.rationale: Loops are allowed; vectorisation is a performance preference.
It produces the same result, just faster.

options.text: Vectorised code always uses less memory
options.rationale: Vectorisation can use more memory; the main benefit is speed.

items.explanation: Correct: MATLAB's array operations are implemented in fast compiled routines, avoiding interpreter overhead per element.
